Ah, MechWarrior. I think MWO is great for what it is. The graphics are pleasing and the various 'Mechs handle just like they should. The game doesn't ask for much with system specs either, most half decent potatoes can run this game at low with at least 30 frames. I've been a long time supporter for MWO and they've added a lot. Things like new game modes, 'Mechs, maps, modules, weapons, different physics, you name it. The game isn't pay to win either (like a lot of people say) more of pay to get your stuff faster because you're lazy type of game. The two main currencies in the game are the C-bills and MC. You earn C-bills how you would expect, playing matches and are rewarded with more if you did well and less if you didn't do well. You earn MC by paying real money for it (something like $14 or $15 for 1,500 MC). With C-bills, you can buy everything with except cosmetics (EX: Christmas lights for your cockpit and such). With MC, you can also buy everything, including cosmetics.
If you're a long time MechWarrior fan, I would give it a try. But, if you arent, I would consider this:
- 'Mechs handle like tanks do. Your mech will walk in the direction it's legs are pointing, not the direction you're looking.
- 'Mechs are also multi-ton war machines the size of a building, they're slow and have a heavy feeling to them
- MechWarrior is a slow paced game, you can't just run around the map getting kills left and right. It requires you to actually think before you do, and stratagize with your team. (No respawns during matches)
For a guy like me, this game is awesome. It's great graphics and low specs means i can play it on my laptop when on the go, and it's multi-player based gameplay is perfect for fun matches with my friends. Addictive and action packed.

This is a preliminary review, after the first chapter.
I really suck at action games, so I was very glad to discover one that has an "story" mode that depends more on stealth than on shooting everything in sight before you die horribly. Even in that mode, this is not an easy game. So far, I die on average several times each at each enemy group envcounter, which happens dozens of times per chapter. Fortunately, the last save is seldom far behind, especially if you do frequent manual saves. Still, a lot of patience and trial and error is required.
Pro:
- Engaging story line.
- Beautiful, smooth graphics, with modest graphic card demands.
- Great voice acting.
- Good controls (if somewhat complicated).
- Lots of depth for action junkies.
- Good controller support (but see Con below).
- 2 autosaves + unlimited manual saves.
- Fast Load time.
Con:
- Gamepad controller support is broken in the introduction, so you have to do that part with KB+M (takes an hour or so, depending on how much experimenting you do - cut cenes in this ection are not skippable). You can switch to a gamepad controller at the start of Chapter 1.
- Controls are not obvious, and the tutorials are optional and incomplete. The help screen for gamepad controller mode is buried several layers deep in Settings. Tip: take a screen shot of the help screen and keep it handy. Do the intro at least twice, and view every tutorial presented, especially if you have not played any earlier games in this series.
- Even in story mode, this is a difficult game, if you are not a whiz at action games.
- The game is quite linear (at least through chapter 1). Side quests are minimal, and easy to miss.
- Lots of long cut scenes (some of which are not skippable on repeated attempts). Fortunately, you can almost always save just after each cut scene, before interesting things start to happen.
- In a living room context, at higher resolutions, some text (e.g., closed captions) is unreadable even in gramepad controller mode. (Why the developers fixed the pixel size of this stuff, rather than its relative size, is incomprehensible.)
- Inventory management is likely to be a major issue after chapter 1 (TBC).
Be warned: unlike some hybrid games (e.g. Mass Effect), this is NOT an RPG in any sense. This game is all about action/stealth. If you take that out, what's left is not much more than a visual novel.

Endless Space is Civ5 in space instead of on a planet.  If you like Civ5, you will like Endless Space.  If you do not like Civ5, you will not like Endless Space.  It has a steep learning curve for the uninitiated, matches can take well over 10 hours at times, and it has the same nuances (for better or worse) as Civ5.  The ES community is also much smaller and answers for many questions which new players may have are not as easily found, but I do not think that this game was made with non-Civ players in mind.  I enjoy this game very much, but I like "boring" macro and micro sims like this.
Do not buy this game for its alleged space combat, because you will auto-simulate most battles if your purpose is winning, and the battles when not auto-simulated are mostly unpredictable rock-paper-scissors-other element-second other element in formula which do not let you control it like the screenshots may indicate.  This does not make this game bad at all, but it also does not make ES a space combat game, either.

There are already dozens of reviews here that are funny, but don't really provide much information about the game - so I'll try to provide a "factual" review, for readers who are curious about the game's actual content. :)
"Zombitatos" is a very crudely constructed "Choose Your Own Adventure" game. It shows you a short video clip, and then prompts you with 2-3 choices. Typically one of these choices will advance the story, while the others lead to death - you then have to restart the chapter, and repeat all the choices you already took, to get back to the point where you failed.
There are less then 10 choices to make, so the game is extremely short. I "solved" it in about 20 minutes (don't draw any conclusions from the "playing time" that Steam shows; like most people I let the game idle in the background to collect the trading cards). There is also an introductory chapter which plays differently - more like a very simple, very linear point&click game, where you see 5 screens and just have to click the right spot on each. But that part is even shorter than the main part of the game, so it has hardly any impact.
The video clips show two guys, a single prop (a revolver), and various urban backgrounds. That's it. The "acting" is ... well, there isn't any. These are just two guys who mechanically repeat some lines from a terribly written script, and laugh when they think they made a joke. Since 90% of the jokes aren't even funny, it doesn't really work, and the only thing that drives the player forward is a morbid curiosity about how much of their cretinous ineptitude the designers are willing to put on public display.
How to rate such a game? I won't say that "this should never have been made", because let's be honest - when we were kids or teens, and had access to a camcorder, smartphone, or anything else that could shoot a video clip, didn't we fool around with that too? Posing as "actors" in something we deemed fun at that time? I know I did, and several of my classmates did ... and that's exactly what "Zombitatos" is: Two teens fooling around with game design and filming equipment, apparently enjoying themselves, and either oblivious or just indifferent towards the fact that the outcome is, by any objective standard, embarrassing crap.
Unfortunately though, the designers decided to offer the result of this fooling-around as an actual game, they are advertising it as a "comedy point & click adventure with puzzles" and they are asking money for it. They present this product as if it was an actual adventure game that they had put any effort into. And at this point, when customers are asked to pay money based on an obvious misrepresentation of a crappy product, my goodwill towards teens "just fooling around" comes to an end.
So if the the designers sell this product as a game, they will have to live with reviewers treating it as such. And as a game, it fails completely. The "story" is an incoherent mess of some half-arsed common concepts slapped together without rhyme or reason, the writing is atrociously bad, the acting is devoid of any skill or talent, the game design is crude and shoddy, the "choose your own adventure" part is structured in the most mindless way possible, and the extreme shortness and lack of content show that the designers did not even _try_ to create something even remotely worth someone's money or time.
Side note: As these guys are obviously very young, and at least somewhat interested in game design, I would like to believe that they'd use the coming years to develop some skills and produce something actually worthwhile. There _are_ a few faint sparks in the game that hint at talents which could be built upon - e.g. a feeling for comedic absurdity (the "Those are good shoes!" joke was actually funny, and one of the few instances where comedic timing was actually present and done right), or self-irony (when the designer made fun of his English as a French Canadian). If the designers were willing to develop some skills, get some quality control, and - most of all - put some actual effort in, then I believe they _could_ eventually be able to produce something actually worthwhile. However, what we currently do - by buying this game, and perhaps even writing a funny fake positive review - is to just encourage them to put out more crap. They can probably earn a few hundred bucks from game bundles, trading card sales, and the occasional Steam sale, and at their age, that might be a big deal. So, since we have rewarded them twice now for putting out crap ("Kimulator" and "Zombitatos"), they probably have little incentive to change that.
Put it on the shelf next to two other timeless classics. Bad Rats and Bad Rats Show.

To start, the port of the game is acceptable. The game's highest resolution setting is 720p, and the graphics certainly aren't very impressive for a 2009 PC game. InFAMOUS looks better on PS3 really, and it came out at the exact same time. I played this game with a controller, so I can not tell you if the mouse and keyboard controls work well. The controls with a controller are alright. They aren't as precise as I'd like, but their good enough to keep the gameplay enjoyable. I experienced a couple crashes, but the game was fairly stable overall.
The gameplay is better than the port and is a nice bit of mindless fun. You can slice, throw, crush, and consume people by the dozen. The homicidal maniac within the player will have a blast butchering helpless soldiers for quite a while. However, eventually your inner homicidal maniac will realize there's nothing else to do but kill kill kill, and he or she will begin to grow tired of the indiscriminate mass murder. You'll probably reach this point before you finish the game, especially after half the enemies become super soldiers, large mutants, tanks, and various other enemies that will knock you about stunning you constantly and throwing you around like a baseball among a group of American children. Getting around the city is quite enjoyable. There's just something satisfying about jumping 50 feet into the air and gliding around New York, but this also begins getting old with time.
The story is forgetable, but if you're buying a game where you play as a superpowered mass murderer for story, then you're clearly looking in the wrong place.
This game fills a good few hours with hack and slash joy, but outstays its welcome. I'd recommend you get it on sale.

I have an EVGA 1070 superclocked, 16GB of RAM and an FX-8350 processor, and can only get 60 fps if nothing is happening. During intense missile trades i'm in the teens or 20s guaranteed every single time.
The game is extremely grindy. Granted, at first you are given the in-game currency "C-bills" at a substantial rate that slowly decays over the course of 25 matches, but after that, best case scenario, you're getting 150k a round. And that's if you win and do really well. Mechs and high-end weapons cost
of C-bills.
Microtransactions. They're everywhere, and expensive. Doing a 3-color skin pattern on a SINGLE chasis you own with a decal and cockpit ornament is easily $20. There are also "champion" and "hero" mechs that cost upwards of the equivelant of $30-$50 of the premium "mechwarrior credits". Not sure if these are any better. I haven't heard anyone claim this is pay to win...yet.
The game also has a system in place where you get "general EXP" and mech chasis specific "EXP" as you play. GXP can be used across all mechs you own to level them up via a "skill tree" while EXP is attached to the chasis you were using while gaining said EXP. Here's the kicker. As you go through the "Basic, Elite, and Master" skill tiers, there is a paywall of sorts. Once you unlock all of the "basic" skills of a single chasis, you are thenthat required to get all the basic skills of MULTIPLE other chasis of the same mech before progressing further in the skill tree of your main mech. WTF? So, of course, your options are drop $50 on the game, or grind for 100s of hours to be able to afford a few more slightly different versions of the mech you already have.
You can also convert your mech specific EXP to GXP at a rate of 1 MC per 25 EXP. Of course, this could have been implamented with C-Bills, but why not add another microtransaction amirite?
"Faction play" was a big selling point of this game. It came 3 years late, and was mediocre when it arrived. The concept is cool but nobody plays it.
CS:GO style "crates". Yeeeep.... Every game thinks this is a great idea now I guess. I'm not 100% sure if you can buy these outright. I have recieved 2 thus far for free. After each round one random player is given one. Then, you must purchase a key to open it. Inside is a random cosmetic, comsumable, or sometimes mech. Don't kid yourself. It's just gambling, and should be illegal to include in games.
At it's core MWO is a fine game, but it's held back by head-scrath worthy microtransactions and poor optimization. If you can't wait until 2018 for MW5, and just have to scratch that battletech itch, this game will get the job done...provided of course that you can stomach the above 5 points...

This game has a very mixed audience, and for good reason. Where most games are based on either following a plotline (like Assassin's Creed) or an arcade-style, keep going back to do better (like TF2), Blockland is entirely different.
Overall:
Though this game has definitely gone extremely far downhill since around 2010 when it was at its height, it still is quite a fun game to play with a couple other people, as long as the game is well understood.
Important aspects in playing Blockland:
If you're to really appreciate the game, you have to have an insane amount of creativity (as in a larger scale of creative than Creative Mode in Minecraft). If you absolutely loved Legos and building brand new creations off the top of your head, this is quite literally that. It's important to note that "worlds" are not randomly generated like in Minecraft. You're given a clean slate and you have to start from rock bottom to build whatever you have in mind.
Also imperative to understand is that this game will not be anywhere near as fun without people you know. To be completely honest, the online community is very very hostile, and it won't be at all fun to play with random people. One could really go on for hours critiquing the community. HOWEVER, if you buy this game with two or more friends, then it can be really quite fun. Combining the creativity of everyone to build something incredible is always a blast, and I highly recommend it.
This is less important, but essential to having quality gameplay; addons are a must. The default weapons, tools, bricks, and events (basically very simplified programming) are a very limited few, and downloading addons will add greatly to the experience. Where you might find yourself limited without addons, adding them raises the bar exponentially, to a point that there is basically no limit. [Also note: addons are completely free and can be found online, likely on forum.blockland.us (in reality just Google them)]

Tiny Story Time: The first time I started playing blockland was a few years ago, before it even came out on steam. The game was fun, nice people, nice servers, a pretty great game!
Then maps were removed...
Then the renderman disappeared....
Then most good players started leaving.....
Then the updates stopped......
Then nothing was left except for
roleplay servers.......
And then the game was dead.
There's just no point in buying this game anymore.

This is truly an excellent product! Whoever needs a cheap, good controller and whoever wants to play PC games with a controller or just wants a controller, this works! The only negative is that finding a good position for your hands takes some time, but aside from that, everything is great! The ability to remap and customize the buttons is so nice and gives the player so much more control, and is so detailed, that you stop thinking "How many options!" and start thinking "How many more options there could be!". The trackpads emulate a real trackpad, analog sticks and dpads really well. The haptic feedback work really well,too, although... sometimes I haven't found it fitting.
However, since many games don't natively support the Steam Controller, setting it up can take up a fair bit of time, and finding the best options takes time. Not much, but some. Also, and here I may disagree with many people, the community is not the most reliable source of bindings. Neither are the developers, I've found some games in which the official bindings can't even start the game. Some bindings also lack keys, for example, in Rocket League, the functions normally bound to Q and E aren't mapped to any button, but you can obviously change that. I recommend asking friends for a binding that works. What you need to beware of, and Valve, please fix this issue is that saved bindings don't alway load, and when you're offline, the bindings revert to the default instead of keeping the autosave. Sometimes, when you connect the controller before opening Steam, you also need to connect and disconnect the controller (in-game) for the bindings to load. Regarding Ergonomics, Buttons and such I can only say: It is really good, however, many may disagree, partially, I think, due to many people using very different controllers for a long time, and therefore not familiar with the controller. I, however, never used a controller before, so this works for me.
Overall, I recommend.

A TOP ALL AROUND GAMERS REVIEW OF THE STEAM CONTROLLER (PROS&CONS)
Let me start by introducing myself, my name is Patrick Sommer, I am a top all around gamer from Denmark, who has been gaming ever since I was 4 years old (I am now 24), starting with multiple old consonoles and moving up from there. I have also been playing competitive eSport for many years on a high level, all things from CS 1.6, Unreal Tournament, Quake, TF2 and more. So, to get to the point..
PROS:
- Comfortable
- Very well designed (buttons, soft/full pull function, touchpads with touch menu etc.)
- Allows you to literally play on a top level, against others who use K&M (Keyboard and mouse)
- Worth it

To start, the port of the game is acceptable. The game's highest resolution setting is 720p, and the graphics certainly aren't very impressive for a 2009 PC game. InFAMOUS looks better on PS3 really, and it came out at the exact same time. I played this game with a controller, so I can not tell you if the mouse and keyboard controls work well. The controls with a controller are alright. They aren't as precise as I'd like, but their good enough to keep the gameplay enjoyable. I experienced a couple crashes, but the game was fairly stable overall.
The gameplay is better than the port and is a nice bit of mindless fun. You can slice, throw, crush, and consume people by the dozen. The homicidal maniac within the player will have a blast butchering helpless soldiers for quite a while. However, eventually your inner homicidal maniac will realize there's nothing else to do but kill kill kill, and he or she will begin to grow tired of the indiscriminate mass murder. You'll probably reach this point before you finish the game, especially after half the enemies become super soldiers, large mutants, tanks, and various other enemies that will knock you about stunning you constantly and throwing you around like a baseball among a group of American children. Getting around the city is quite enjoyable. There's just something satisfying about jumping 50 feet into the air and gliding around New York, but this also begins getting old with time.
The story is forgetable, but if you're buying a game where you play as a superpowered mass murderer for story, then you're clearly looking in the wrong place.
This game fills a good few hours with hack and slash joy, but outstays its welcome. I'd recommend you get it on sale.

Human Revolution is a Shooter/ Stealth game with heavy ammounts of RPG elements that asks you to make some major choices, like do you want to play it as a stealth or shooter for example.
This is a well polished, well put to gether game and everything  you excpet out of a AAA game.  The game play is engrossing.  The options given to you seem meaningful.  The world is well crafted and expansive (while not open world, the use of large hub-worlds is even better givning the player space to explore while still keeping the game focused).  Finally, the story is strong enough to get you engaged.
And all of this is true, at least at first.  Human Revelution though, is a game that suffers the further you proceed and really collapses in on its own wait.  Not to undercut how wonderful this game is, but there comes a point where the gameplay stops to be compelling, the choices seem pointless and the story becomes downright stupid.
As bad as all that sounds, I still think this game is almost a must play.  The game works so well for so long that I highly recommend it.  The fact that it falls apart at the end doesn't take away from how strong it starts.
It's not a game I recommend you finish, but considering the large ammount of play time you can squeeze from it; that is all right.  Find some time to play this game.

I got into Blockland back in 2005 when I was just 11 years old, and back then it was a free game that looked just like Legos, and ever since then, I've seen people and friends come and go, rivalries with other games that were only similar in the concept of 'sandbox game where you can build and destroy anything'.
As someone who had practically no social interaction prior, this game and it's community actually helped me grow and mature as a person, I've met so many cool, intelligent, talented and funny people over the years and even became friends with some of them, and it got me in to basic C++ scripting, 3D modeling, audio editing, and even a bit of video making. It is at this point that I feel like I owe my life to this game. Even to this day, I find myself coming back to this game every now and then to build something, to create a new mod, try out someone else's mod, or to just goof about on servers.
This game, for me, and several others, is like the 'Hotel California' of video games, you may leave, you may stop playing for a while, but you always come back, for one reason or another. Even those who don't like this game or it's community and get banned for their actions keep spending more of their money just to come back, it's like a drug that you just can't quit!
For the 11 years I've been at this game, I've been very active on the message boards, and it's been such an interesting, funny, and unique community over the years, and I've been able to watch it grow and change as time went on, like, I've never been so invested in a community as I am with Blockland's.
I do hope that Blockland becomes as popular as games like Roblox, some may disagree with me on this, that they prefer this smaller and more controlled crowd of people, but Blockland really does deserves a bigger audience, it actually is a fun and amazing game. It may be slow and tedious to build something big and amazing, but that's how building is with every sandbox game, "
.", and if building isn't your thing, there's just a big variety of gamemodes and servers out there that are PvP death-matches, role playing servers, a boss battle server, knife fights in the sky with grappling hooks, dog fights, single-lap races, multi-lap races-- there's just so many to choose from, you're bound to find something you like!
The biggest problem with the game is '
', what time of the day you get on matters, what time-zone you live in compared to other people matters, what day of the week it is matters, time is a big factor in finding busy and/or good quality servers.
While I recommend this game, I also commend checking out the message boards, there you can chillax and talk amongst others that play the game, get help with the game, post pictures of things you built or did, download add-ons or other sorts of mods that people make, or just talk about whatever else, about other video games, or about drawings or other sorts of creative things you or other people do!

This controller was designed with an extremely ambitious goal- make mouse+kb games playable on your couch, along with other console-friendly games. As a side goal: make the most customizable controller in existence. I think it succeeds on both fronts, though it has to make some compromises along the way. Whether you like this controller depends on whether you can tolerate those compromises, as well as how badly you've been missing what it offers.
So what does it offer?
- Mouse-like precision in games! This really shines in FPS games, or else third-person games with point-and-shoot elements. If a game accepts both gamepad and mouse input at the same time, you will feel like you are cheating it's so good.
- Crazy customizability: you can tune every single thing you could think of. Mode-shifting allows for a dizzying number of possibilites. Want to enable gyro for precise aiming, but only while crouching and pressing the shoulder button more than 75%? Yeah, you can make that happen.
- Some developers have really embraced it, with custom control schemes that let you tune different control layouts for in-game menus, live action, etc. Even if the developers ignore it, the community picks up the slack.
- Regular firmware updates in response to user demand. The controller has only gotten better over time.
- Good integration with the Steam Link. Plug it in and hit the Steam button, and you're off to the races.
Now the bad stuff:
- The touchpads dominate the face of the controller, pushing the ABXY and joystick buttons closer together. There's no getting around it: it makes the controller feel more awkward than competing gamepads. You will either get used to it, or you will rage-quit the controller because of it.
- The controller has a steep learning curve. Until you get a good 6-12 hours of use with it, you will probably suck at some of your games a little.
- You can map mouse, kb, and gamepad controls at the same time (i.e. everything is mapped as a gamepad, except your right touchpad is a mouse). Some games do NOT like this, and they will freak out unless you are 'all gamepad' or 'all m+kb'. In those situations, it's easiest to map full m+kb controls to the controller, so you can keep that sweet, sweet mouse-look. Trying to use the touchpad in "joystick mode" sucks.
- If you alt-tab a lot, or if you minimize your game often, you can get some quirky behavior where your controller isn't focused on the right thing. This has gotten better with updates, but it still bites you every so often.
Overall, I like this controller... though I find myself using it for specific games, rather than as an all-rounder. It's great for games that require a lot of analog aiming, or else games that allow simultaneous gamepad and keyboard/mouse input. You do have to invest some time and effort to learning the controller, to get the most out of it.

This is my first Naruto game ever, and I have to say I enjoyed it quite a bit. The game has plenty of content, it was nice to relive the war, and the adventure mode provided some new experiences of the story. I did have a few issues with the game though, specifically slow downs due to FPS drops. I highly recommend that you check your PC specs with the one listed in the store page, prior to buying this game, especially if you want to play in the 60fps mode. If you do encounter such as issues, the common solution is to turn off aliasing in Naruto, and enable it via Nvidia Control Panel (or Catalyst). Make sure the game is running with GPU and not your iGPU, especially if your a laptop user. For desktop users, changing your 3D settings in Nvidia to preferring high performance, will be very beneficial for the 60fps mode. Other than that, lets get deeper in the review.
Pros:
•The story mode covers about 5-8 hours worth of gameplay, with very fun boss battles.
•Adventure mode adds a new variety with free roaming, questing, and allows you to experience things not seen in the Shippuden anime.
•VS has many options that will keep you enaged, from survival matches to local 1v1 multiplayer.
•Fluid controls and mechanics
•Tons of content
•Has different cinematics, from stand still images of the show in certain scenes, to recreated scenes via the game engine.
•Character interactions in a fight, is pretty entertaining, some character react uniquely to others.
•Has a huge roster of characters to choose from, and with team based gameplay, the amount of combinations is huge.
The game has so much content, that it would be difficult to blow through it quickly. The story mode allows you to relive the events in the anime, while the adventure mode brings you to experincing the Hidden Leaf and many other locations across the world. Across the adventure mode, you will find plenty of sellable items that are used to customize a character. For VS, you have the ability to enter tournaments, or survival matches, where you can choose your own team and go head to head with other predefined teams, or 1v1. However, there are some bad points to this game.
Cons:
•As mentioned earlier, this game does suffer from slowdowns if the fps drops.
•Performance isn't quite good to begin with.
•Lip sync is horribly off for dub.
•Like the anime, too many flashbacks. I wished Adventure mode would be new stories, but most of it was flashbacks.
Aside from that, the overall content is bountiful and the replayability is extremly high. I highly recommend getting the "Road to Boruto" dlc, as it expands on the Adventure mode, by offering more new stories and relives the movie.

This is an extended review about Prototype, so before starting, let me sai it short. This is a very cool game, but full of bugs and glitches in the Steam version. I bought it on sale, and I suggest doing the same thing. Now, let's start with the extended review.
STORY/GAMEPLAY: This is a sanbox game. very unique in its kind. In spite of being the typical delinquent who wants to rule the mafia, the main character is a human infected by a special virus that allows him to absorb other living beings, and mutate part of his body. There are a great deal of "natural weapons" to use, and also the environment is pretty much destroyable, with the exception of building. The story in my opinion is the shining point of this game, and the funny thing is that it's not explained at all in the beginning, but it's revealet little by little through special events (that last far over the "main story", if you want to collect all pieces of it).
The free roaming is quite good. It's cool being this spiderman-like character, and desn't get boring over time.
GRAPHICS: Graphics are average. The main character and the cinematics are quite pretty, but the rest sucks pretty much. There are 10 to 15 "characters" in the game, so the world feels pretty monotonous and dull. The building are quite monotonous too, put together with a little variety. Despite this you can feel some slowdown when there are many enemies on the screen, even if you have a last generation video card.
BUGS: If I understand correctly, this is an xbox/ps porting, so it's full of bugs and glithces. Looking on the internet you can manage to fix pretty much everything, but still sucks having to "open new game > return to main meny > load saved game", or else the game crashes.
AI: Artificial intelligence just sucks. After just a couple of hours of game you can perfectly predict what will happen, even what moves your enemies will do. I think that you can pretty much expect it from a sandbox game, but the overall scarce variety of character is quite dull.
I think that's all. To sum up, this is a short list of pros and cons.
PROs:
- very good story
- feels incredibly cool
- complete it 100% is quite challenging
CONs:
- bugs
- AI
- graphics (i put in the cons because of the overall effect, and the slowdowns)
That's all. Hope this review is helpful.

For people who always watched Star Trek and wondered, "What would it be like to be on a starship bridge?"
The best answer to that question comes in the form of Artemis.
You network at least 3 computers together to form the bridge, and each console becomes  a different station, i.e weapons, comms, helsmen, etc.
The more people you have per starship bridge, the better. If you have enough for two crews, you can do a pvp match or co-op.
The Stations:
Captain: Tells everyone what to do
Helsman: Essentially the chauffeur of the ship.
Weapons: need I say more?
(The minimum you need for a bridge is captain, helms, and weapons.)
Engineering: Diverts power and coolant to give systems a boost and also prevent the ship from exploding
Science: Scanning enemy vessels for weaknesses and scanning space for potential threats
Comms: The secretary of the ship. This is the station you give your girlfriend because you want her to help, but you don't want to give her anything important. Even though I say that, it does come in quite useful- it's really boring to play, however.
That being said, I highly recommend this game for Star Trek fans and non-trekkies alike, but only if you have a group of friends that you can do it with.

I am a die hard strategy game fan and have played many, if not all, strategy games on steam or elsewhere. Now the mame Endless Space is a worthy name for the game. For it really is endless fun, an endless hours worth of effort which reaps endless amount of joy, (if you dont mind a bit of hard core strategy action every now and then with indie games)
.--------------------------------PROS------------------------------
1.The game has a Hero system which distinguishes it from other strategy base building games. The plus side is you're not bored after long while playing this game,it adds variety to the game play, slightly opens up the multitude of outcomes, and gives a sense of control to the players which is unmatched in the entire game.
2.The tech tree is unique in that it has four varieties: diplomacy, applied sciences, military, exploration. Each has its own flavor. Military provides might, diplomacy gives keys to diplomacy, applied science sometimes reveals new resources or helps in development of a star system, exploration lets you colonize new planets and star systems. Together they give a unique blend to the game play.
3.Exploration of the galaxy is fun for any newb or experienced player alike
---------------------------------CONS-----------------------------
1.Some technolgies hold the key to survival. For example if you dont discover wormhole travel you cannot travel to other planets or star systems, similarly if you dont discover applied technologies you are more then likely not going to discover hidden advantages of certain resources.
2.The game uses a point system for rating players. Problem is, once your points overtake any of the A.I.s the A.I. attacks you where you're more than likely to lose the war. So its advisable to move ahead of the pack
All in all its a 6.5/10 and definitely worth the buy, if you can handle a bit of warfare maneuvers from the A.I. and have the spirit to colonize the galaxy.

It is not a bad game, but it isn't a good game either, so I'll give a thumbs down.
First of, there is nothing innovative about this game, it basically feels like Civ, but in space, with some weird/counterintuitive mechanics.
For example:
The combat is basically autoresolve, but with cards you can play. Those cards buff your fleet or debuff the enemy fleet and different card counter each other, on paper it sounds not bad, basically some sort of rock-paper-scissor system. BUT! There are so many cards and some cards even counter itself, that rock-paper-scissor becomes some weird thing where paper can suddenly counter scissors and rocks are a stupid thing to use agains scissors.
Another thing is restricted fleet sizes. You can up the fleet size through techs to 22 Points (different ships use different set of points, for example Battleships use 2 Points, Dreadnoughts use initally 4, after a techupgrade 3). This leads to:
a) rushing the techs for bigger fleets (Most of the time Bigger Fleet > Smaller Fleet)
b) Quality of Ships > Quantity of Ships (Point a is still valid, but you can't zerg a superior ship with 20-30 Ships)
Overall I would recommend rather to play Sword of the Stars (The first one, not the second), instead of this game.
Good Points of this game are:
Somewhat pretty graphics
Easy to get into/Hard to master (mainly because many things are somewhat explained poorly)
Nice Lore (All the alien races are somewhat interesting)

Nunca pensei que um shooter tão bom poderia ter elementos de RPG. A princípio parece ilógico, mas o sistema de evolução de Renegade lhe permite jogar o jogo relativamente curto de diversas maneiras distintas. São 03 as classes de atributos dos upgrades de seu veículo armado, defesa, ofensiva e táctica, este último se trata de um poder especial único de cada personagem. Você tem o limite de usar apenas 04 upgrades ao mesmo tempo. A personagem Roxy por exemplo tem um poder especial devastador, uma chuva de mísseis que devasta boa parte do cenário, mas esse poder pode ficar ainda mais assombroso se você usar mais 04 upgrades nele, aumentando seu poder ou raio de ação por exemplo, isso muda completamente sua forma de jogar, pois mesmo com um personagem frágil ainda assim com paciência, escondendo-se e esperando o tempo necessário para resfriar seu poder especial, seu personagem continua sendo mortal e perigoso. Ou se preferir, pode deixar sua personagem mais equilibrada, adicionando dois upgrades de defesa e dois de ofensiva, sem evoluir o já poderoso poder especial, assim sua forma de avançar no jogo muda radicalmente, você já tem condição de partir para cima dos inimigos sem ficar tão dependente do poder especial. Agora multiplique isso por 07,  quantidade de personagens (veículos), e multiplique mais uma vez por 12, quantidade de fases disponíveis, contando as DLCs e vc perceberá que esse "pequeno" jogo na verdade tomara muitas horas de sua vida.
Os gráficos são um show à parte, a visão distante e superior permite enxergar uma riqueza imensa de detalhes, como o voar de pássaros, o levantar da poeira do chão na passagem de um helicóptero. Efeitos de iluminação detalhistas impressionam nas fases noturnas, explosões fenomenais mais se assemelham a um espetáculo de pirotecnia e a sensação térmica e destrutiva passada pelos efeitos de chamas  é de cair o queixo.
O jogo é charmoso, e a história é contata no formato de desenhos em quadrinhos feitos à mão, exatamente como em uma HQ. O que para mim é um sonho, visto que cresci lendo gibis, e sim, isso muito me agradou.
A jogabilidade funciona muito bem no controle do 360, onde o analógico esquerdo  move o veículo enquanto o direito move a mira, permitindo um dinamismo raro na maioria dos shooters de se mover e atirar em direções diferentes. É uma pena não poder dizer o mesmo do teclado e mouse onde fica mais complicado dirigir o veículo, e é uma pena também o jogo não oferecer suporte a outros controles, apenas ao do 360.
Mais a melhor parte deixei para o final. O multiplayer, tanto splitscreen (offline) para até 02 pessoas, como o online para até 04 pessoas é muito divertido. Na verdade como todo bom shooter deveria ser, o jogo deve ser jogado preferencialmente no multiplayer cooperativo onde as campanhas podem ser terminadas mais facilmente. Tentar zerar o jogo sozinho no Hard é penoso, você vai querer a ajuda de um amigo. Sem falar que alguns personagens foram criados pensando exatamente nesse modo, como Crystal, que emite um campo de força de energia grande o suficiente para proteger você e mais 03 amigos das balas inimigas.
De falhas o jogo tem um bugs irritantes, como por exemplo a exigência do caríssimo controle do 360, o que é absurdo visto a simplicidade da jogabilidade do game, e absurdo maior ainda, não poder jogar o modo cooperativo local com dois  teclado/mouse wireless por exemplo, e mais absurdo ainda não poder  jogar esse mesmo modo com um teclado/mouse e seu amigo com o controle do 360... OU SEJA, VC PRECISA COMPRAR DOIS CONTROLES DO 360 PARA APROVEITAR ESSE JOGO AO MÁXIMO. É o recado da Avalanche Studios para os seus fãs...

The Steam Controller might be the only controller I've ever enjoyed using. In the past I have tried Xbox 360 Controllers, PS3 Dualshock Controllers, Xbox One, a few 3rd party, and even a Wiimote (still use it for games via Dolphin). Just couldn't enjoy using them. I am someone who grew up as a PC gamer, and kb/m feels natural, but unfortunately, it's clunky as hell in the living room, hence the controllers. What I personally love about the Steam controller is the things most people who grew up with controllers dislike: The trackpad-like control pads, and the upward curvature of the arms, it feels oddly natural and familiar to me. The other part I love so much about this controller is how customizable the controls are, and how easy it is to make the adjustments on the fly. However, all the praise aside, the controller has its faults. The general build quality feels like that of a prototype, better plastics certainly could have been used, better noise reduction (you can hear the haptic feedback clearly) , as well as small adjustments in the size of controls (mainly scaling the trackpads a little bit down, and the x/y/b/a buttons up a bit). Also, the controller is not for anyone who isn't in to customizing and configuring their gaming experience. If you want plug and play, steer away from the Steam Controller, it just isn't for you. If the rest of the features I mentioned sound like a controller you'd want, and you don't mind the listed cons, go ahead and get it.

Besides, usually you accidentally talk to somebody or pick something up so that they let you walk in the front door, and you wonder what all the vents and roof access is for.

To start, the port of the game is acceptable. The game's highest resolution setting is 720p, and the graphics certainly aren't very impressive for a 2009 PC game. InFAMOUS looks better on PS3 really, and it came out at the exact same time. I played this game with a controller, so I can not tell you if the mouse and keyboard controls work well. The controls with a controller are alright. They aren't as precise as I'd like, but their good enough to keep the gameplay enjoyable. I experienced a couple crashes, but the game was fairly stable overall.
The gameplay is better than the port and is a nice bit of mindless fun. You can slice, throw, crush, and consume people by the dozen. The homicidal maniac within the player will have a blast butchering helpless soldiers for quite a while. However, eventually your inner homicidal maniac will realize there's nothing else to do but kill kill kill, and he or she will begin to grow tired of the indiscriminate mass murder. You'll probably reach this point before you finish the game, especially after half the enemies become super soldiers, large mutants, tanks, and various other enemies that will knock you about stunning you constantly and throwing you around like a baseball among a group of American children. Getting around the city is quite enjoyable. There's just something satisfying about jumping 50 feet into the air and gliding around New York, but this also begins getting old with time.
The story is forgetable, but if you're buying a game where you play as a superpowered mass murderer for story, then you're clearly looking in the wrong place.
This game fills a good few hours with hack and slash joy, but outstays its welcome. I'd recommend you get it on sale.

Pros:
-A unique and beautifully world. All NPC (even background ones) have voice, and some special NPC have their own animation scene when talking
-The idea of creating and evolving a god of your own sure is interesting
-You can (in a way of speaking) played all classes.
-The gameplay of all classes is fun, and unique ( compare to themselves and to other games)
-A surprisingly great story (for a MMO)
-Open-world maps, with a good mission system and story within each
-A close-to-non-target playing (it isn't entirely non-target, but it's actually have active dodging, and a combo-style gameplay that make an illusion of nontarget playing and overall, of fast action gameplay)
-The overall strength of character isn't entirely rely on equipment
-The skill-tree, building and mission types system is really fresh
-God system really is god system, you'll have to gather followers to worship you, and you can send them to do something or off on a journey to spead your ideal and faith and with more faith, you 'll get stronger (you'll have to earn their faith by doing quest too, a very real god system i must say)
So if you bother enough to read this far, right now, you might think: This game as far sounded like a really interesting one, so why? Yeah, that's the reason i first played it 2 yrs ago, and now, is the reason why i dropped it after 2 wks returned.
Cons:
- If you are in the same situation as mine and want to get back in the game through Steam after 2 yr+, i must warn you: you can replace or combine the Steam account with your old
account from before. If you don't want to replay so many hrs, don't bother return. If you aren't, proceed below.
-You will be overwhelm by how many kind of currencies you need in this game, and in some way they can be grind, but still, with a game that doesn't have any crafting (up until the time i wrote this review) that was too much, and also means that you have to grind, hard.
-The drop system for the equipment, which hard to understand first but then eventually found out, is broke. It's rely on the Might, the overall strength indicator of this game. That mean, if you ain't got enough Might, no matter how hard the mission you gone through, now matter how many tries to achieved it, no mater how rare that piece of equipment, you'll only got the ones fit with your might and no more). Some might say it fair. I thought so too, but the problem come from the others too.
-The Might system is also the problem. The Prestige is your level, and even though after less than 10 min of that night I've gone straight from 47 - 74 pretige after achieved my God form, I realized that Prestige isn't the main factor of the might, too. And also the Prestige isn't up by grinding quest. So basically grinding won't help you "level up", and also "level up" won't help you get much stronger nor better equipment. Some too might say this still fair, then come the problem with getting Might
-The Bastion, the Cathedral (i called it Church for short) and the Tower of Knowledge (ToK) is the main source for Might. They level up by using your resource (Church and ToK) and doing some specific quest (Bastion), and the higher they are, the higher the Might bonus you might recieve. The problem is, first, those resource need either grinding hard, or buying using another type of resource (Argent). And you can still receive Argent from ingame. Some based on that and say this game is grindy but not P2W. But guest what? You can buy a LOT of them with Argent, and Argent can be bought with real $. That mean you can easily got a LOT stronger in a LOT shorter time than grinding. And since this is classic RPG, got stronger fast meaning very much. And know what? These constructions, they have daily limited for the amount of resources you can contribute, but you can get over it by Stimulants, a resource specifically to "skip" through anything, and you can get a small amount of it through some basic activities in game, or just BUY it using Argent. And I can guarantee to you guys, you can't get enough Argent for all this just by farming ingame. Oh, I forgot to mention that the higher the constuction is, the higher the resource and stimulants for it'll required? Yeah, that mean, the more you give, the much more you get stronger compares to those grinding peasants like me. I remembered when i was playing this before, it isn't that much cash grabbing as it is right now. There were limits for sure, but not as much.
-You won't get classes and talent for each (a way to called skill in this game) for free. You'll get 3 first basic, 1 more after the 2nd province clear , and 3 more after complete the main map line through all province. I wouldn't say anything if it's all, but then you need to grind hard for 5 more classes (actually 6, I got Outlaw thanks to Steam Welcome Gift but, I fell bad for newcomers in original server right now) and it's not easy. Before, you used to get all the classes with just complete the first main mission in all provinces and now that ain't gonna happen anymore. And also, before the 1st season story uses to be the main maps line and up on complete that, you 'll get all the reward but now, they split it in to "Stories Tab" and forces people to play it again for 1 costume? But back to the grinding, you will need 25k Spark of Transformation (let's called it SoT) to unlock a locked class, and the only places to farm it is through the 5-man raid, which was impossible for 1 man to solo since the boss all way got about a few xxxxxxx times than your health and even a normal thug or minion with less than 1 heath bar can f*** you up. Nothing to say if i can find a good team, but the community (at least in NA server) is THE S****IEST. I have sit for 5 min until i can get a team and the guy just dumped us because we were all new gods with less than 100 Pres level, even though with a gen 7 equipment set and 200k might he could just carried us, and we wouldn't have any attention of letting him carry us all and tried to help him the best we could ( i even wasted 1 divine change - cost a lot at low level - to help) and no one care about the public matchmaking. The 5-10 man raid is also the main source for high quipment as we said, even though equipments isn't the main strength, it's dead important after you get a god form if you want to go higher. That means in order to get higher equipment, you have to get Might and Prestige lot faster. And the most efficient way to get it is ... well now you know.
So that mean though 4 system, they've made a systemically, intentionally failure that makes newbie incredibly harder if not almost imposible to go further, unless paying a little more, and also a big gap which can't be filled between richs and farmers. Some might say since all resource can be farmed, it's not P2W. After this, you will decide if it's true or just another beautiful lie. And it's important to say that at the time i played this 2 yrs ago, all of this didn't happened. This game got good potential, and it used to be great, but not anymore. Since it got all the beauties of an unique MMO, I truly encourage to just try it's a few hr, but after hitting that wall, well, it's your choice. With me, I just got enough.

I really am not one who bothers writing reviews, but I'm going to go out of my way because I feel people have been a bit too harsh on this little title. Let me be clear now, it's nowhere near perfect, and has the misfortune of belonging to a genre that is already oversaturated and filled to the brim with imitators, which means it has to compete with a huge amount of similar games, including a lot of well-made indie ones. But if you don't go in expecting the level of quality you'd want from Megaman or Cave Story, you might be pleasantly surprised.
And whoever said Megamari is better than this... huh, just no, not even close.
Let me get the worst part out of the way. First, the English translation is honestly terrible. And sadly, not even in a "Pokemon Vietnamese Crystal" laughable sense, but just in a "you can sort of understand what they're saying if you read it enough times" way. It also suffers from... technical problems, as in, the dialogue sometimes goes outside the text windows, which makes it even harder to understand. It is kind of sad, because the story seems to be basically a pastiche of '90s anime: the dialogues and "plot twists" really remind me of Sailor Moon, Rayearth or Shinzo, and one of the bosses is a winged Josuke Higashikata. No, seriously. And the gratuitous japanese used for the names is so ridiculous it's almost charming. Point is, it's not anything you'd want to take at face value, and could be enjoyable in its own way if it was better presented. Then again, I don't even know many who cares about the story in this kind of games and I don't see how it would be worse than "go defeat Wily one more time".
Two, the secrets are hidden in completely obtuse parts of the stages. I get they're
to be hidden, but... really, some of them are pretty much impossible to discover on your own, and their location doesn't even make sense at all. A similar problem arises for the endings requirements, which aren't as obvious as you might think at first. Those weren't, in my opinion at least, good design choices.
Lastly, there are some minor bugs. Nothing gamebreaking (which is already more than enough for a low-production value indie title), but you might get the character stuck in a certain animation or randomly get semi-permanent use of the shield at no cost (which is actually super useful). The sprites and camera also slightly tilt around or occasionally flicker during cutscenes, which might be a bit annoying, but it's tolerable IMHO.
The 8-bit music is ok. There aren't any particularly memorable tunes, but no earrape either, and most of the tracks are at least fitting enough.
Same with the sprite art, it's more or less on the level of Momodora III. Charas and enemies aren't super detailed, but are not abominations either, with Himari's sprite being pretty cute IMHO. As for characters portraits, don't expect anything on the level of Rosenkreuzstilette, but hey, this guy probably didn't have a hentai artist helping him, so cut him some slack. Their designs are quite cheesy, but as I said, it's not a very serious game anyway.
The other "neutral point" is the challenge factor. To put it simply, Taimumari is (relatively) easy and short, with the only hard task being the no-powerup achievement. This is especially notable in the first 4 main stages, as not only can you essentially skip all enemies by jumping and dashing, but all bosses use very predictable patterns with obvious blind spots.  You also have extra lives, and even if you do end up getting a game over, there are some checkpoints so that you don't always have to start from the very start of the level. So yeah, if you're looking for Meat Boy ragequits, you won't find them here, and I'm kind of surprised to see other complaining about it being too punishing. But regardless, I don't believe this to be an inherent flaw, as it makes the whole thing more relaxing and, you know, fun to play. Plus, the learning curve is pretty smooth, with later stages that require you to make full use of your abilities, and if you really want a challenge, the dev later added a free DLC level which is infinitely harder anything you'll encounter in the main game. You can also choose the difficulty, so in the end, you get what you ask for.
The controls are extremely responsive. No input lag, and your character has great mobility, with double jump, dash and wall jump from the get go, which improve the platforming and ensure stages will never feel too long.
There is a wide variety of abilities, both in terms of spells (you have a Kamehameha, a thing that throws light yo-yos around, a bomb, an overpowered homing projectiel and so on) and special moves (you can slow down time or even rewind it, and you get a very useful shield for the enemy bullets), so anyone can chooses what best fits his own playstyle. The game expects you to learn to use these mechanics, and slowly ups the difficulty so that you never get to be too comfortable.
The power-up system allows you to buy increased health and mana meters, or to strenghten your attacks, and while it can get a bit grindy, it also greatly helps those that might find the game too hard for their own taste.
The level design is much better than some reviews would make you think. Granted, you're not gonna see anything you've never seen before, but there is a pleasant amount of diversions to keep the journey fresh, like some sidescrolling shooter segments, a "mountain-climbing" part, or an area where enemies and obstacles only move if and when you do. Also, I was happy to see that annoying mechanics like the old disappearing blocks did not appear here. You'll still have to deal with instakill spikes, but hey, that is to be expected, and there are very few instances where the platforming might get a bit frustrating. Enemy positioning also isn't that bad, you'll almost never get hit by something that you could not see or be forced to ram into a foe to avoid falling into a bottomless pit. The overall longevity of the stages is just right, going from 3 to 10 minutes if you try to get S-rank for the achievements; a complete first playthrough shouldn't take more than 3-4 hours depending on how many times you die and how many collectables you're trying to get, but there are a 2 extra endings, each with its own final boss, to make it a bit longer.
Finally, the game is still receiving minor updates and additions. Always sad to see little titles completely abandoned, and it's nice that it hasn't happened here yet.
It's not the greatest 2d platformer ever, and indeed, there are a lot of admittedly better alternatives, including even free ones (Khimera: Destroy all Monster Girls being a good example). The writing is shoddy at best, and incomprehensible at worst, the plot is as campy as Batman & Robin, the programming could be improved, and for a game inspired by Megaman, it's not that hard either. Still, I can see the effort put into it, the presentation is cute and nice-looking, it's far smoother and more playable than a lot of similar low-budget productions, and above all, it's just quite fun to play. Considering the low price point and all that, I liked it quite a bit. If you're forced to choose between this and Cave Story+, definitely go for the latter, but if you're a fan of 2D platformer and happen to have some spare change, consider trying this one, as IMHO it's definitely worth it.

Taimumari didn't have too bad of a start. The movement didn't feel awful and I was willing to overlook the shoddy writing. Things went downhill fast when the combat was introduced, though. First of all, whenever you attack, the camera immediately comes to a halt; attacking repeatedly, as you will when you're fighting, can be a bit nauseating as a result. But even disregarding that, the combat just doesn't feel good. There's no sense of your attacks connecting since enemies don't appear to get knocked back or have i-frames when hit. Because of this, I felt discouraged to use melee attacks in comparison to magic, which requires MP that recharges over time just a bit too slowly for my taste. There are only a few required battles though, because most enemies you can ignore and jump over — though that does mean missing out on currency used to level up your stats at the shop. I'm bored just thinking about this.
I went through a few levels and found that a majority of the maps were just rectangles with enemies on them, with light platforming in-between. Not very interesting to go through. There were also some cutscenes and whenever a poorly-written message popped up the screen would jitter for no reason. Collectibles are hidden throughout the levels and sometimes they're within walls that you have to jump into at a right point to get them but the collision is really awkward at these parts so I ended up clinging to air a lot before finally getting in there. One time I died after dying because a projectile was under my dead character. The 8-bit soundtrack became grating. I fought two bosses and both of them were not difficult nor interesting to fight. After I got a game over in the second level after running out of lives — because this game has a lives system for some reason — I gave up and stopped. I wasn't having any fun.
Taimumari's just janky and unpolished overall. Everything about the gameplay apart from the core platforming controls doesn't feel satisfying, and the story is so poorly worded and uninteresting that there's really nothing to keep you playing. It's bad.

I've been using gamepads since early 90s. I got my first dual-stick controller with vibration feedback when the first DualShock came out for PSOne, and I loved it so much that I bought a gamepad for my PC and have been using it in every PC game with controller support ever since. I'm basically a sad console peasant who ended up being a PC gamer.
Recently I've realized it's time to replace my ancient controller with something with analog triggers and more buttons, and started looking for options available on the market. I had my first-hand experience with almost every controller of current and previous console generation, including some 3rd party ones, and came to know that none of them were perfect for my taste. And so, I've decided to go with a device where innovations outweigh its downsides - the mysterious Steam Controller (hereinafter SC).
I've read a lot about SC's build quality, that it feels plastic and cheap, and was afraid to be disappointed. Imagine my surprise when I grabbed it, pressed all the buttons, moved the analog stick, and found out the build quality and feel is similar to that of an Xbox One controller, and that one is anything but cheap. I'd say SC feels more expensive even.
Ergonomics is great. The controller is big and feels natural in my big hands. Some may find it to be a bit heavy with batteries inside. It doesn't have rubber grips, but then again, only some 3rd party controllers do, and it's not a big deal here because your hands rest so comfortably when you're holding it that palm sweating becomes less of an issue, and the textured grips prevent it from sliding anyway.
I had my big doubts regarding the shifted placement of buttons and the analog stick, but all of them turned out to be within perfect reach from your normal holding position without any additional effort.
The analog stick is convex, which I personally prefer to concave sticks of X360 and XBOne controllers, as when I roll it with my thumb, a convex stick allows me to have a constant surface contact in every position, which is not the case with concave ones. No wonder Xbox One Elite controller comes with convex replacement sticks. The stick itself has a rubber cover with a textured rim, and its resistance is just what I want it to be. Definitely one of the better analog sticks I've tried.
The ABXY buttons are smaller than those in regular controllers, but this didn't cause me any kind of discomfort, I could still hit any button easily without looking at them. Of course, after decades of using standard controllers I had to adapt to new button placement at first, but one day was enough for that.
Right and left bumpers have the same mechanical click and resistance as the 2nd revision of XBOne controller, you can press them across the entire button surface, but heavy button mashing may eventually wear the mechanism out, so you have to be careful with those (FIFA players, I'm talking to you!).
Triggers are pure joy with their dual-stage mechanism, as in, they click after you fully press them. The click serves as a separate button. This is particularly useful in GameCube emulation, as the original GC controller also had dual-stage triggers, and many games made use of that functionality. Trigger travel distance is rather small, but the resistance is just right. They are placed a bit lower than bumpers, which helps keeping fingers more relaxed when you press them.
Right and Left Grip buttons located at the back of the controller are great additions, they're very convenient to press and hold, and work great for features like enabling gyro control.
Gyro is an often-overlooked feature of SC, but it's actually an asset that provides an extremely high accuracy that can exceed the one of the removed right analog stick, and compensates all the possible awkwardness standard controller users may feel from switching to a trackpad. The only downside is that currently it's only possible to use 2 gyro axes as analog inputs at the same time, while a third one will act as a threshold for activating digital buttons. It's nothing Valve can't fix in one of the future Big Picture updates, however.
And last but not least, the very things that make SC unique - two trackpads. They have a nice texture, both can be pressed, making a rather loud click. Left Trackpad usually works as a D-pad, while Right Trackpad replaces the 2nd analog stick, and in conjunction with gyro totally outperforms it.
Another little bonus feature many people fail to mention that was a pleasant surprise to me is a built-in speaker that makes funny PC-speaker-like noises when you turn the controller on or off, and it's possible to choose different sounds or melodies from the list, separately for each of those actions.
Rumble was another one of my concerns, as I'm used to powerful rumble motors of DualShock controllers and love the extra immersion it provides. SC features haptic feedback motors, making trackpads vibrate when you touch them or slide a finger across them. These same motors are now also used to emulate a standard rumble feature, and the result is very similar, but less shaky. Overall it feels more like heavy scratching rather than shaking, but it's actually stronger than I thought it would be, and provides a very similar experience to regular gamepads.
SC requires Steam to be running, and a game has to be launched via Steam. It's not a problem for a heavy Steam user like me, but some people may be annoyed. These people may be happy to know there's a 3rd party software called GloSC that provides a system-wide X-input emulation and Big Picture overlay layer for the SC. Steam still has to be running in the background though. I thought one of the downsides of the SC would be the inability to use it in UWP (Windows Store) games, however with GloSC it's actually possible now! That's one downside less.
Now that Valve has added support for all the available controllers out there, you probably already know how powerful Steam's controller configuration module is, and if not, go check it out! Everything is configurable and rebindable, double-presses, long presses, turbo, mode shifts, dead zones, action sets etc. etc. So I'll only mention SC specifics.
Trackpads can be used as sticks, mouse, d-pad, scrollwheel, button pad, touch menu - you name it! I was afraid SC will be bad for playing old-school 8- and 16-bit 2D platformers. However, it's possible to set trackpads to work as touch d-pad and buttons with haptics. Once you do that it becomes surprisingly convenient - you can button-mash all you want without damaging the controller, the response is great, and the virtual buttons are big and familiarly placed.
Mouse and keyboard games work great, particularly RPGs and MMOs where a touch menu can be used to turn a trackpad into a virtual button panel with all of your skills - you just click or touch it in a place where the virtual skill button is located.
In racing games, you can use your SC as a wheel thanks to gyro, or use a trackpad, which is still more precise than a stick for a smooth wheel-turning (hardcore racers use racing wheels anyway).
For FPS and other games that require precise aiming - trackpad for direction and gyro for aim correction work wonders.
The only real downside here is the learning curve, it's very steep, and almost every game requires individual approach. To those who feel lazy to learn all the configuration nuances, community configs are there to help making it a plug-and-play experience.

When you compare SC with other controllers, don't forget that it's a multifunctional device, and its new features can actually replace the old ones you're used to. What you see as downsides can actually turn into advantages once you feel how it all works together. I used to think Xbox One Elite was the best controller out there, but now if I'm given this choice, I'd rather take two Steam Controllers.

Every bit as fun as the old tech demo I loved ten years ago.  Now in a new and improved form.  Lots of action, lots of guns, lots of enemies, lots of blood on the sand, Crimsonland is a wonderful top-down shooter in the old "Smash TV" play style.  Waves of enemies trying to overrun your defenses.
Obviously this game has changed a lot since the early versions.  New game mode, different enemies, more weapons, perks, etc. have only enhanced the experience for me.  There's a lot to do.  My biggest complaint would be that the four-player multi-player is local co-op only.  Given that this version is on the Steam platform, it would be amazing if you could hook up with players on your friends list to really go at it.
That doesn't make the single player any less exciting however.  There's a lot of things to unlock through the missions (and they appear to have added leveling to the missions, unlike when I was playing it on Steam earlier, which does make the missions a lot more fun as well), as well as several extra modes to choose from.
The price IS a bit high for my liking.  I'd probably recommend it more when it goes on sale.  If you do get a chance to pick it up them, don't let it pass you by!

CRIMSONLAND is the ultimate brainless videogame, a pinnacle in time wasting engineering. Buy the developers of this a beer.
Its a top-down, plotless shooter in which you gun down hordes of zombies, spiders and reptilians. You start out with an awful pistol but killing enemies will randomly dropped unlocked weapons with different effects, power, range and accuracy. Some of these weapons require some semblance of thought but there are others like ION LASER CANNONs and HOMING MISSILES and ION LASER HOMING MISSLES where you can just click wherever you see movement and BOOM! Everything dies.
To make things even funnier (read: easier) there are also a bunch of powerups that drop, which can do things like make your gun faster and more explode-y, or freeze everything on screen in ice cubes, and- my personal favorite- generate a nuke aoe that just kills everything around you. The killing power of the drops effectively incentivizes throwing strategy to the wind and running in guns blazing to a mob of well over 100 enemies to set off a chain reaction of random projectiles and explosions, killing everything en masse. There is NO strategy involved, and barely any skill at that, but HOLY♥♥♥♥♥♥its so goddamn fun!
Like a triple layer enchilada full of meat, cheese and cheese-stuffed meat, CRIMSONLAND adds even more chaos with "perks" that tie into a leveling system. Having fun generating large aoe windmill projectiles? Well, you can also have a perk that randomly shoots bullets in all directions every time you reload! Things getting a little close for comfort? You can make your body poisonous so that any monster that attacks you dies!
The developers were courteous enough to add extra modes and such, like a mode where you rely only on powerups and a regular survival mode. There's also probably the closest thing to skill-based gameplay in the mode where you're only alllowed a shotgun and then swamped with an enormous horde on either side. Holla @ my high score on the leader boards (its somewhere in the 4000s!!)
This is a really fun game overall. Hours of replayability in the campaign alone (two unlockable difficulties) and tons of different ways to play it. Video games do not actually need to be thought provoking to be fun. Score one for FUN and THE SECOND AMENDMENT, you liberal arts school hipster trash!

This was a great top down shooter.  The graphics impressed me throughout the entire game.  The cars are fun to drive (controller definitely recommended), and destroying/exploding everything in sight is very gratifying. Renegade Ops is a 4 players co-op dual stick vehicular action shooter where players are given a choice of vehicles and is played from a top down perspective.
Vehicle handling is very smooth and the combat is fast and explosive. A gamepad is highly recommended tho. The visuals look very impressive with lots of details. Music and sound are equally good. It also features a level progression in which you can earn EXP Points to enhance your vehicle.
Downsides, the main campaign is very short at only 5 hours across 9 missions. The Coldstrike DLC adds only 2 more missions and felt that it should've have been in the main game itself. There are no checkpoints per mission and with the limited amount of lives given, it can be frustrating when you die. Also, unless you have a native XBox360 PC Controller, you will need to download a special driver for use with other gamepads.
Overall Rating: 7.5 / 10

I hardly ever write reviews but here:
The primary issue with Taimumari is that it's constantly hit and miss.
It's obvious there's inspiration from Megaman in this game, but it seems they overlooked the technical aspect of what made the gameplay so solid in megaman games, this game could be a real gem if it had all the kinks worked out and if it had more polish.
To provide an example, there's a point where you're running from a machine and the screen is panning, you've seen a scene like this in many platforming games probably.
Well while on this moving screen if you attack or dash, the camera follows that action rather than staying centered where it was.
And if you throw an attack that trails on the camera will follow it which will result in you dying because you can't see what's going on where you currently are.
There's a boss fight involving this same concept later in the game, and for some reason it doesn't have this issue there, it being fine for the boss fight where the screen is also panning but not for the part earlier in the game is a good example of how Taimumari is hit and miss.
I haven't beaten the game and I probably won't, I'm on chapter 3 of the final area of the game, if you beat it, congratulations.
it's playable, but don't expect to get through it without getting frustrated by technical limitations.
Also just so you know, you have a double jump but unlike other games with double jump, walking off of a ledge will act as if you've expended both of your jumps and you'll just fall to your death.
And that's my review for a game that's already been out for a year

The trackpads feel really comfortable and intuitive to use to me, and I've never used a laptop trackpad or anything like that before, I have fairly larger than average hands though so maybe that's why some people have trouble with them, at first the sensitivity was a little low for my preference, but it was very easy to up the sensitivity.
3. I personally like the analog stick better than the 360's analog sticks, I prefer the convex shape and the slightly smaller size, though I can understand that it may be a con for some.
4. The A B X Y buttons are smaller and in a different place than the 360 controller, which again may be a con for others, but I personally prefer them over the 360's, it will take a little getting used to the different position of the buttons, but it's not a big deal. Also the 'paddle' buttons are really nice.
5. The customizability is amazing... I guess some people are too lazy or don't have the time to fiddle around with customizing the controls for each game, but I love tinkering with stuff.
6. I really like the haptic feedback when it's on low, but only on low.
7. The gyro is a really neat feature, and surprisingly accurate, I haven't tested it a lot yet though.
8. It plays a little tune when you turn the controller on or off :D.
Cons:
1. The batteries are a little tough to put in.
2. The haptic feedback on medium is a bit louder than I'd like, haven't even tried high haptics.
3. For some reason they decided to put a glossy part on the front of the controller.. The biggest con for me, I hate fingerprints haha.
Neutral:
1. Doesn't really have vibration, there is an option somewhere for 'experimental vibration' or something like that, but it's basically just using all the haptics at once. I don't mind since I usually had vibration turned off on my 360 controller anyways.
2. The construction isn't really cheap as I see a lot of reviews say, but it's not premium quality either, It feels comparable to the 360 controller. It has a better textured grip, but some of the buttons have a 'clicky' sound, I don't mind since it just sounds like a mouse click, but some might not like it.
3. Had a problem at first where the left half of the right trackpad didn't work, but I went to the controller settings and clicked the calibrate button and that fixed it.
Ok that's about it for now, I will try to remember to update the review in a week or so once I get a bit more familiarized with it, if I figure out anything else I like or dislike about it anyways.
